evidence: Parent AC-1: 'init/mount, create, claim, transition, and the push/fetch reconcile path all succeed against it ... Verified by an opt-in live integration test that drives those verbs against a real ephemeral bucket and asserts a second clone reads the writes back.'
Parent decomposition: 'Docs + ADR ... Delivers AC-4 (docs half) and the AC-1 operator-facing configuration.' — only the configuration/doc slice, not the live end-to-end test.

Child 0289 live canary is scoped to the heal path only: 'an opt-in live canary ... exercises the same happy path [heal_multi_bundle] against a real ephemeral bucket' — not the init/create/claim/transition/push-fetch verb set.
Children 8970 (fail-closed CLI tests), 2b05 (pure unit), and b014 (docs, 'No code, schema, or test changes') deliver none of the AC-1 verb-set live test.
findings.finding: Parent AC-1's tested outcome — an opt-in live integration test that drives the full verb set (init/mount, create, claim, transition, push/fetch reconcile) against a real ephemeral S3 bucket and asserts a second clone reads the writes back — is owned by NO child. The parent decomposition assigns only 'the AC-1 operator-facing configuration' to the docs child (b014), which is docs-only and runs no test.
findings.location: child b014-1526-16d0-4c3f (and the parent's child-decomposition line assigning AC-1 to it)
scenarios: Completion verifier checks AC-1 and finds no test exercising the full verb set + second-clone readback against a real bucket; only docs and the heal-path canary exist.
The end-to-end 'ticket data resides only in the SSE-KMS bucket, never in GitHub, and a second clone reads writes back' assertion is never actually executed by any child's oracle.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the pip-install string across 2b05 (_install_hint), 8970 (AC + CLI oracle), and b014 (docs) to one canonical form (the emitted `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`).
evidence: Child 8970 AC: 'a single actionable message naming pip install '.[s3]''; testing oracle: 'prints the message naming pip install '.[s3]''.
Child 2b05 AC: 'the standard one-line message containing the exact string pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]''; approach: '_install_hint ... emits pip install 'nava-rebar[<extra>]''.
Child b014 AC: 'install (naming pip install '.[s3]' ...)'.
Child 8970 approach: 'calls rebar._optional.require_s3_helper(), letting its actionable error propagate' — so the emitted string is 2b05's nava-rebar[s3], not .[s3].
findings.finding: The pip-install string that AC-2's fail-closed message must name is inconsistent across siblings. Child 8970 (which delivers AC-2 by propagating require_s3_helper()'s error) and child b014 assert/document `pip install '.[s3]'`, but child 2b05 — which owns the actual message via _optional._install_hint — asserts and emits `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`. The message 8970 surfaces comes from 2b05's seam, so it will read `nava-rebar[s3]`, contradicting 8970's own AC and b014's docs.
findings.location: child 8970-40af-1785-4530 (AC-1/AC-2 message assertion) vs child 2b05-fcb5-7e87-41d9 (message source) and child b014-1526-16d0-4c3f (docs)
scenarios: 8970's CLI subprocess test asserts the output contains `pip install '.[s3]'` but the propagated require_s3_helper() message contains `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`, so the test fails.
An operator follows docs/s3-backend.md's `pip install '.[s3]'` but the runtime error tells them `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'`, or vice versa.
findings.suggested_fix: Standardize on the string _optional._install_hint actually emits — `pip install 'nava-rebar[s3]'` — in child 8970's ACs/oracles and child b014's docs, or explicitly override the propagated message; do not assert two different strings for the same seam.

findings.checklist_item: Specify how the AC-1 ephemeral bucket is created and torn down (unique name, guaranteed delete/empty in test teardown even on failure) so the live test leaves no orphaned resource.
evidence: AC-1: 'an opt-in live integration test that drives those verbs against a real ephemeral bucket'
No teardown, bucket-lifecycle, or object-cleanup step is named for the ephemeral bucket — an ABSENCE against the T10 reproducible/teardown check.
findings.finding: The AC-1 opt-in live integration test provisions a 'real ephemeral bucket' but the plan does not specify its teardown/lifecycle, so the stood-up test resource has no guaranteed cleanup contract.
scenarios: A failed or interrupted integration-test run leaves an orphaned bucket (and KMS-encrypted objects) accruing storage cost and clutter across CI runs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ground the `git-remote-s3>=0.3.2` minimum pin by citing the specific helper release/changelog that introduced the IfNoneMatch per-ref lock (or state how the pin will be verified), so AC-2's fail-closed threshold is provably correct.
evidence: Plan asserts helper 'below the pinned minimum' must fail closed and pins '(`git-remote-s3>=0.3.2`)'
Retrieved release-history search for git-remote-s3 returned no version/changelog data corroborating that 0.3.2 is the first release with the IfNoneMatch lock
Plan grounds the lock's existence in a live experiment but does not tie the IfNoneMatch capability to a specific released version
findings.finding: The minimum-helper version pin `git-remote-s3>=0.3.2` is asserted as the floor that contains the IfNoneMatch per-ref lock (the mechanism preventing multi-bundle state), but the plan provides no grounding for why 0.3.2 specifically is the correct minimum; this is a load-bearing capability assertion for AC-2's fail-closed-below-pin behavior.
scenarios: A helper version >=0.3.2 that predates the IfNoneMatch lock is accepted by the guard, still allowing multi-bundle corruption
The pin is set too high and rejects a valid helper, breaking AC-1's working-remote path

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the non-interactive merge conflict-resolution protocol for the auto-doctor (e.g. how event/ticket file conflicts are reconciled) so the 'no event discarded' guarantee is achievable without an interactive prompt.
evidence: 'merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock and collapses them to one bundle'
AC-3 requires 'every commit/event from all divergent heads is reachable from the healed tip (no head or event discarded)'
A non-interactive git merge of divergent orphan-branch histories can hit conflicts; the resolution strategy (union of event files, ours/theirs, append semantics) is unstated
findings.finding: AC-3 / the Auto-doctor child specifies 'merges all divergent heads' non-interactively but never states how merge CONFLICTS are resolved when two divergent heads touch the same ticket/event data — a load-bearing data-design decision for an autonomous merge.
scenarios: Two divergent tickets-branch heads modify the same ticket file or event log and the auto-doctor merge encounters a conflict

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Place the init/mount-time s3 helper guard in the shared store engine seam (the mount/init *_core path) rather than only _commands/init.py, so library and MCP ingress inherit the fail-closed check.
evidence: Plan: "wire that guard into src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_commands/init.py so s3:// remotes fail closed when the helper is missing/old"
AC-1 names "init/mount" as verbs that must succeed via the library/MCP surfaces, not only the CLI
findings.finding: The fail-closed helper guard's init-time enforcement is placed in the CLI command surface (src/rebar/_commands/init.py). AC-1 requires init/mount to work across all client shapes (library, CLI, MCP), so a library facade or MCP handler that initializes/mounts an s3:// store without routing through _commands/init.py would skip the init-time fail-closed check. The push.py placement is a shared seam and does inherit across surfaces, but the init/mount guard does not.
findings.location: Child decomposition → Preflight enforcement: "wire that guard into src/rebar/_store/push.py and src/rebar/_commands/init.py"
scenarios: A library consumer calling the mount/init core function directly (not the CLI init command) sets up an s3:// store with a missing/old helper and only discovers the failure at first push, not at init — the init-time fail-closed guarantee is bypassed.
An MCP tool handler that initializes/mounts a store reaches store setup without passing through _commands/init.py, skipping the init-time helper-version guard.
findings.suggested_fix: Move require_s3_helper() into the shared store mount/init core function that all three ingress paths call, keeping _commands/init.py responsible only for CLI error-message formatting.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify in the auto-doctor design how the heal enumerates and fetches BOTH `<sha>.bundle` heads as merge inputs (not just the helper's single-bundle fetch) and how it collapses to one bundle atomically — including what happens if a concurrent lockless writer re-creates a second bundle during/after the heal — so 'every commit/event from all divergent heads is reachable' is guaranteed and the state actually converges.
evidence: Plan: 'on detecting the multi-bundle signature during push, merges all divergent heads under a repo-level repair lock and collapses them to one bundle'

Problem statement: multi-bundle = two `<sha>.bundle` files; `git ls-remote` returns the ref at two SHAs; the helper's normal fetch resolves a ref to a single bundle, so 'merge all divergent heads' presupposes a way to fetch/enumerate BOTH bundles' commits locally that the plan leaves unspecified

The 'repo-level repair lock' is a LOCAL lock; the multi-bundle state is created by fleet clients lacking the IfNoneMatch lock, so a local lock cannot prevent a concurrent writer from re-adding a second bundle during/after the collapse — a check-then-act (heal-then-push) that can be racing
findings.finding: The auto-doctor merge-heal (AC-3) does not specify how it obtains BOTH divergent heads as merge inputs, nor how it atomically collapses to a single bundle without a concurrent lockless writer re-creating a second bundle mid-heal.
scenarios: Healer merges under a local lock while another lockless/legacy client on a different host pushes a fresh bundle, re-creating the multi-bundle state immediately after the collapse

Helper's fetch picks only one of the two bundles, so the 'merge' silently merges one head with itself and the divergent head is never actually incorporated — violating the 'every commit/event reachable' guarantee

findings.checklist_item: State that the documented IAM policy MUST be least-privilege — S3 object read/write limited to the configured prefix plus KMS encrypt/decrypt on the specific CMK, with no wildcard (`s3:*`/`kms:*`) grants.
evidence: AC-4: 'SSE-KMS bucket + CMK/IAM setup ... are documented'
The plan names IAM setup as a documented item but never states the policy must be minimally scoped or wildcard-free — an ABSENCE in an infra-configuring plan the T10 least-privilege check targets.
findings.finding: AC-4 requires the CMK/IAM setup be documented but does not require the documented IAM policy be scoped to least privilege (S3 object read/write on the configured prefix + KMS encrypt/decrypt on the specific CMK), nor does it forbid wildcard/admin-for-convenience grants.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC-4 / Docs + ADR child
scenarios: Operator copies the documented IAM example verbatim into production and grants s3:* / kms:* because the doc did not model a scoped policy.
findings.suggested_fix: In the Docs child's IAM section, ship a minimal example policy scoped to the bucket/prefix ARNs and the single CMK ARN, and explicitly call out that broader grants are not required.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile how `sync.remote` carries the S3 target: either relax `_as_git_remote` (_config_coercion.py:142) to accept an `s3://` URL scheme, or specify that `sync.remote` stays a git remote NAME whose configured URL is the s3:// value — and assign an owning child; AC-1/AC-2 currently assert the value itself is the s3:// URL, which the existing validator rejects on '/' and ':'.
evidence: AC-1: 'rebar uses an s3://bucket/prefix value of sync.remote'; AC-2: 'When sync.remote resolves to an s3:// URL'
src/rebar/_config_coercion.py:142 `_as_git_remote` rejects a value containing '/' or '..' (line 153) and any char in `_BAD_REF_CHARS` (line 155)
src/rebar/_config_coercion.py:115 `_BAD_REF_CHARS = set(" ~^:?*[\\\x7f")` — includes ':', so 's3://bucket/prefix' is rejected three ways (':' , '/', and no '..' but '/' alone suffices)
src/rebar/_config_schema.py:643 wires `remote` through `_as_git_remote`; _config_schema.py:350 documents it as a git remote NAME not a URL
git-remote-s3 conventionally attaches the s3:// URL to a NAMED remote, so the plan may intend sync.remote to stay a name — but the ACs assert the value IS the URL, leaving the mechanism un-reconciled
findings.finding: The plan's core integration premise — that `sync.remote` holds an `s3://bucket/prefix` URL value — is contradicted by rebar's own config validator, which rejects such a value.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria AC-1 / AC-2; Context ('pointing sync.remote at an s3://bucket/prefix remote')
scenarios: An operator sets `sync.remote = s3://bucket/prefix` per AC-1 and the config coercion raises ConfigError before any push/init runs
The AC-1 live integration test cannot even load config with an s3:// value

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the AWS credential-resolution + KMS grant precondition the git-remote-s3 helper requires at push/fetch time, and confirm the detached async-push child (push.py:185) inherits that credential context (or route it to the preflight/docs child).
evidence: The plan states SSE-KMS/CMK/IAM setup is DOCUMENTED (AC-4) but never states the runtime precondition that the helper must resolve AWS credentials + KMS decrypt/encrypt grant to push/fetch

src/rebar/_store/push.py:185 launches the async push as a detached `python3 -c` child with `start_new_session=True`; whether that child inherits AWS credential context (env/instance-profile/SSO) is a live integration precondition the plan does not address
T3(c): auth/HTTPS preconditions must be stated for an external service integration; S3+KMS is exactly such a service
findings.finding: The AWS credential-resolution and KMS-grant precondition that the git-remote-s3 helper needs at every push/fetch is not stated as an integration precondition, and its interaction with the detached async-push child process is unaddressed.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria (all); Child decomposition 'Preflight enforcement'; Out of scope
scenarios: Async push child (sync.push=async) runs without inherited AWS creds and the s3:// push silently fails as PUSH_PENDING
CMK grant missing decrypt for the fetching identity → fresh clone in AC-1 fails at bundle download
